title: Introduce cost-aware token economics bench and throughput calibrator
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: teams increasingly optimize for cost-per-token as well as latency; existing benchmark harnesses measure latency and tail quantiles but do not model token-level economics across batching, quantization and cache hit patterns. This PR adds a reproducible benchmark and a lightweight throughput calibrator that quantifies cost vs latency trade-offs for common inference strategies and outputs standardized CSV/JSON summaries suitable for the reporting pipeline.

What this PR introduces: a) bench/cost_econ/runner: a runner that synthesizes request streams with configurable sequence-length distributions, session affinity, and cache-hit models, instrumented to track token counts attributed to model variants, quantization level, and batch size. b) bench/cost_econ/calibrator: a sweep driver that runs multi-dim experiments (batch size, max-seq, quant-level, kv-cache-enabled) and produces normalized cost metrics using a pluggable cost model (supports our hosted rate card and a local nominal model for private deployments). c) reporting/cost_econ/transform: lightweight processors that aggregate runs into cost-latency curves, per-token unit-cost estimates, and a rollup JSON for Redwood Console ingestion. d) example workloads and README: a short tutorial showing how to reproduce a regional sweep and how to feed results into Optimize.

Why it's different: unlike previous throughput-focused runners, the calibrator models token economics: accounting for wasted tokens due to overpadding, impact of prefix caching, and cost delta from quantization. The output is intended to drive two downstream use cases: (1) automated Optimize recommendations (batch/quant profiles) and (2) SKU/capacity planning for Dedicated pools.

Scope of changes: small, self-contained additions under benchmark-lab with no runtime changes to the serving binary. The calibrator reuses the existing workload harness and telemetry collectors to remain compatible with the ingestion pipeline.

How to run locally: ./bench.sh cost-econ --config examples/sweeps/hosted-small.yaml --out-dir /tmp/cost-run; the README contains a one-liner to upload results to the reporting topic.

Metrics and expected stability: example runs in CI (see attached matrices) show stable p50/p95 latencies within 5% of baseline when batch sizes are < 8; cost-per-token delta tables are produced for each sweep and include confidence intervals across 5 repeats.

Notes: this is intended as a baseline generator for Optimize; the cost-model is intentionally simple but pluggable. Future follow-ups will add more sophisticated spot-price modeling and cross-region arbitrage simulations.

review_comments: Leo Martinez: Can we expose kv-cache hit-rate as an output dimension so Optimize can learn a policy? -> Author: yes, added an explicit 'kv_hit_rate' field in the run schema (calibrator and runner).
Priya Nair: The cost model should allow a per-region multiplier for cloud egress and reserved capacity. -> Author: added region_multiplier to RateCard and documented how to provide a JSON override.
Samir Kapoor: CI flaked on one run; please add retry and increase repeat count to 5 to get stable CIs. -> Author: increased repeats and added retries in calibrator, re-ran CI matrix.
testing_summary: Added smoke integration that runs a small hosted sweep in CI (approx 3m) and a dedicated smoke run under a mocked rate card. Tests assert stable latencies and presence of per-token accounting fields; CI matrix added for nightly longer sweeps.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on schema compatibility in reporting/transform.py and on the cost_model interface; the runner is intentionally conservative in concurrency to avoid perturbing latency baselines.
release_notes: Add cost-aware benchmarking harness and a calibrator to produce cost vs latency curves; useful for Optimize recommendations and Dedicated capacity planning.
